chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The daughters of the daughter inherit when there are no daughters; they take the place of the daughters.

key_terms.مَكَانَ: In the place of / instead of

ai.seo_question: Do granddaughters inherit if there are no daughters?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the principle of 'representation' (ta'rib) in Shia jurisprudence, where granddaughters through a daughter inherit in the absence of direct daughters, mirroring the share of sons' daughters. It highlights the Shia view that the presence of a daughter excludes her daughter, whereas the absence of a daughter allows the granddaughter to inherit, distinguishing it from some Sunni schools that apply the 'blockage' (hajb) rule more broadly. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Shia inheritance law in ensuring equitable distribution among female descendants when primary heirs are absent.
